author: reek
body: The same quotation a third way. codex/test/quotes-gate.codex proves it through the offered-works blob, codex/test/quote-from-store.codex proves it through the fact store on an attached disk, and this proves it through a peer: the work is on another machine's disk, and the only thing this source has is the digest.

author: reek
body: There is no %%QUOTED-WORKS%% section here and no store attached. The host asks a peer for the work by that digest, and prepends what comes back to the blob before the compiler ever sees the source. The compiler is not told where the work came from and has no way to ask -- which is the point. It hashes the content, checks the signature, checks the key this source pinned, and checks the floor, exactly as it does for a work that arrived beside the source or off the local disk. A peer that lies is refused by arithmetic; a peer that is honest but unknown is refused by the floor. That is what lets the messenger be untrusted, and it is why peer resolution can live in the host rather than in the compiler.

author: reek
body: The trusted key is named here, in the source, and never by the peer. The works arrive over a transport, and a transport must not be able to vouch for its own cargo.
